$comment: Workloads for the memory benchmark. Every browser in a run gets the exact
same URL list in the same order.
Live sites are the honest thing to measure — nobody browses a static
mirror — but they are also the largest source of run-to-run noise: an ad
campaign or an A/B bucket can move a page's memory by tens of megabytes.
That is why the runner interleaves browsers within a repetition instead of
finishing one browser before starting the next, and why results are only
Login-walled sites are deliberately excluded. A signed-out X or Notion tab
measures a login form, not the app, which flatters whichever browser you

baseline.label: Idle (no pages)
baseline.description: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

light.label: Light — 5 text-first pages
light.description: Documentation and text sites with little advertising. Isolates engine baseline.

mixed.label: Mixed — 10 pages
mixed.description: The default. A realistic spread of text, app-like and ad-supported pages.

adheavy.label: Ad-heavy — 6 pages
adheavy.description: Ad- and tracker-dense pages. This is where a network-layer blocker should show up as lower memory, because blocked frames and scripts are never instantiated.

scale.label: Scale — 20 pages
scale.description: High tab count, where Chromium's process-per-site model and Gecko's capped content-process pool diverge most. The interesting comparison against a Firefox-based browser.
